context: One of the nine bundles is this shape, in every clothing: a service returning a server error on a steady fraction of requests and succeeding on the rest, the rate stepping up abruptly. The failing fraction tracks the inputs — some records carry a field, some do not — so a naive read reaches for the input samples, the audit, the request samples or the change log; those are the decoys and show the data unchanged since long before the onset. The cause readings are the release: the deploy ledger shows a new build started at the onset, the diff shows a defensive default dropped, the known-good baseline shows the prior build tolerating the same records, the service log shows the build id flip and the first failing status together. The dressings rename readings and services (suite/families/incidents.py:172); the fraction-of-requests Signal survives them all.
counterfactual: The overshoot is naming bad-deploy from the ledger alone on any error spike: the ledger in every bundle lists a recent deploy, and on a spike whose Surface names an external provider the release is not the cause — the class must be read with the diff, the baseline or the log confirming the regression, and the check fails a wrong class before it reads the citation (suite/families/incidents.py:220).
decision: An error spike where a steady fraction of requests fail with a server error while the rest succeed, stepped up abruptly rather than climbing, on a surface with no timeout storm: it looks like bad input or bad data, and the data-shaped readings — payload or input samples, catalog/inventory audit, request or call samples, record/row change log — are the decoy. The data is unchanged; it is the release that regressed. Open the deploy/release/rollout ledger first (a new build started at the onset of the spike); if a second reading is wanted, open the build/artifact diff (a defensive default dropped or a lookup made strict), the known-good baseline (the prior build tolerating the same records) or the service log (the build id flips at the onset and the failing status begins). Name bad-deploy and cite the release reading(s). Do not open or cite any data-shaped reading, and do not cite one as corroboration beside the ledger: it is not the data, and a data reading cited fails the task however right the class is.
